- Prior documented right lower extremity DVT 5 years ago (established risk factor for post-thrombotic syndrome).  
- Doppler/venous duplex shows venous reflux AND obstruction in both superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg (definitive imaging evidence of post-thrombotic venous damage).  
- Wound culture shows no growth of pathogenic organisms (rules out active infection as primary driver).  
- CBC is normal (no systemic inflammation or hematologic disorder contributing to ulceration).  
- Clinical impression explicitly identifies “chronic venous leg ulcer secondary to post-thrombotic syndrome”.  

[GAPS]  
- Ankle-brachial index (ABI) — needed to exclude concomitant arterial insufficiency, which could impair healing or alter management.  
- Skin biopsy of ulcer edge — required to rule out squamous cell carcinoma (Marjolin’s ulcer) given >3 months’ duration.  
- HbA1c and fasting glucose — to assess for diabetes, a common comorbidity affecting wound healing.  
- Serum albumin — to evaluate for hypoalbuminemia, which impairs tissue repair.  
- Comprehensive metabolic panel — to screen for renal dysfunction (e.g., uremia), hepatic failure, or electrolyte derangements affecting healing.  
- Clinical documentation of CEAP signs (e.g., lipodermatosclerosis, hyperpigmentation, atrophie blanche) — needed for formal staging and prognostication.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Chronic venous leg ulcer due to post-thrombotic syndrome
